topic: When High-NA EUV enters high-volume manufacturing
disagreement: ASML/imec (June 2024) expected High-NA HVM in 2025-2026; ZEISS SMT says series production starting 2025; ASML's 2025 annual report expects the EXE platform to start supporting HVM in 2027; ASML (July 2026) says Intel entered HVM on a subset of 18A layers.
possible_reasons: definition: 'HVM' for a few dual-qualified layers on an existing node vs a node designed around High-NA (Intel 14A)
date of statement: expectations slipped between 2024 and early 2026
ZEISS page undated and may predate the slip
rationale: The annual report is the most formal, audited-context statement; the July 2026 Intel milestone is a narrow use on layers also printable by NXE.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether the first node built on High-NA (Intel 14A, or memory nodes at SK hynix/Samsung) reaches volume in 2027-2028.

disagreement: Korean press (via TrendForce) says TSMC will begin High-NA at 1.4 nm; TSMC's SVP says A14 needs no High-NA and TSMC's chairman says High-NA is owned for R&D but kept out of production on cost.
possible_reasons: press inference vs on-record executive statements
A14 family variants (A13/A12) could change later
source quality: secondary report of a newspaper
rationale: Direct quotes from TSMC executives on the record outweigh an unattributed press report.
remaining_uncertainty: TSMC has not stated a node or year for High-NA production.

topic: Price of one 0.33 NA EUV system
disagreement: SIA/BCG (2021) cite about USD 150m; Reuters (2025) about USD 250m; ASML's 2025 NXE revenue implies about EUR 237m per system.
possible_reasons: population: list price vs average recognized revenue incl. options and used systems
rationale: Derived from audited revenue and unit counts for the same year; still an average, not a price.
remaining_uncertainty: ASML does not publish list prices; options and upgrades blur averages.
